thread:
alex: Proposal: shrink operators admission surface to a tiny "lease" (units + immutable safety_flags + optional drain_ts). runtime decides model_variant and consumes units. keeps operator simpler and centralizes fallback logic in runtime.
maya: Strong +1 for simplicity, but we need clear semantics for safety_flags (e.g. no-quant, min-recall:0.9). runtime must enforce them strictly.
priya: Agree. Also require idempotent redemption API: runtime redeems token_id + delta_units -> operator returns receipt. prevents double-charge on retries.
sam: Observability requirement: every redemption must emit token_id, units_used, variant_chosen, fallback_reason, and trace_id so console can reconcile cost_by_variant and investigate regressions.
ops-bot: FYI last incident: several tenants saw unexpected quant fallbacks when cost-hints flipped mid-request. Link: https://incidents/6901200001 :warning:
alex: Ops datapoint matters. Two practical additions: 1) include drain_ts/grace_ttl in the lease so operator can mark draining without preempting inflight; 2) make safety_flags immutable for the token lifetime.
maya: also add a "preferred_model_family" string so tenants that need deterministic outputs can express a bias. runtime should prefer but still record when it couldn't.
priya: Proto sketch I'll draft: "id, units, expires_at, drain_ts?, grace_ttl, safety_flags[], preferred_model_family?". Errors: TOKEN_EXPIRED, INSUFFICIENT_UNITS, VIOLATES_SAFETY, SERVER_ERROR.
sam: Rollout idea: advisory tokens first (runtime treats flags as hints), canary a few tenants with strict enforcement, dashboard watch for fallback spikes and cost regressions.
alex: Next actions: priya to draft proto + idempotency receipts, sam to add observability panel, maya to list safety_flags we support. Sync tomorrow 9:30 for sign-off.
